reason: The method relies on intraday 3-minute chart breakouts, flag/pennant patterns, order flow and scaling in low-float stocks under $10, which cannot be approximated on daily bars.

universe.description: US stocks under $10, low float, trading at least 2.5x average daily volume

setup.rule: Scan for stocks under $10 with volume >=2.5x avg; watch daily/1h for support/resistance then 3-min flag or pennant after breakout and consolidation
setup.quote: I like to look for stocks under $10 ... stocks that are trading at at least two and a half times their daily average. ... flag patterns or pennant patterns, which are just simple like a like a breakout and then a consolidation.

entry.rule: Wait for breakout then consolidation on 3-min; enter on next push with full size one bullet
entry.quote: After something breaks out, I'm never the first one in into a breakout. ... looking for a breakout, consolidation pattern, and then that next push.

stop.rule: Tight stops; exit immediately on failure or wrong order error via market order
stop.quote: if a trade's not working, I'm not going to let it get to that that max ... just market half out.

exits.rule: Scale out immediately on breakout for profit; reduce to 1/5 size at final target like 200-day MA; cut if not moving right away
exits.quote: as soon as I put on a trade and I get a breakout, I'm instantly selling some shares. ... typically I'm at like a fifth of my size when I hit my final target.

sizing.rule: Full size one bullet per trade; risk aversion keeps potential losses tight via entries/exits rather than fixed %
sizing.quote: I'm much better just going full size, one bullet into my trades. ... I truly don't say um I'm going to risk 2% on this trade

market_filter.rule: Only trade when risk-on; sit out slow days or when too many friends/family chasing; use VWAP for bull/bear control
market_filter.quote: when risk is not on, you really just got to be patient and go for the A's ... If it's over, theoretically it means that that bulls are in control.
